action: Written preservation representation identifying date, location and time window, requesting that control-room logs, wireless logs, CCTV and any body-worn footage be preserved pending disposal of an RTI application.
authority: SSP Patna; SP Katihar; SP Munger; SP Siwan. Four separate representations. Siwan was not in the original list and is the best-evidenced of the four.
method: Speed post where an address is held, retaining the receipt; email otherwise. Only Munger has a postal address in this archive. letters.html fills the sender's details into all four and opens each one in a mail window, addressed and ready to read.
legal_basis: Not a statutory instrument. A representation puts the authority on notice; destruction after notice is itself a documentable fact.
notes:
MOST URGENT ITEM. Drafts for all four are in correspondence/ and are unsent.

CORRECTED 18 September 2026. This item used to read 'No court is seized of the Bihar incidents. Nothing currently interrupts any retention schedule.' The first half is no longer true and the correction strengthens the representations rather than weakening them: the State of Bihar is a respondent in the Supreme Court proceedings on the protests and has filed an affidavit there (PROC-BIH-001, PROC-SC-004), and the Court constituted a High Powered Enquiry Committee by order reported 18 August 2026 (PROC-SC-006). The drafts are addressed on that footing.

The second half stands. No preservation order for any Bihar location is held by this archive (RET-007, UNKNOWN), and an inquiry existing is not the same as a direction to preserve having been made and communicated to a district police office.

Siwan added. It carries CORROBORATED evidence of firearms discharged and injuries, on the State's own affidavit, and had no representation queued. Sitamarhi appears in the PUCL panel findings (INC-BIH-005) and nowhere else, so there is no dated incident record to write from and none is invented; that gap is real.

Munger is UNVERIFIED as to whether force was used (INC-BIH-003) and its draft says so in terms. Do not firm that up.

action: Retrieve an authoritative text of the Right to Information Act 2005 and record the URL actually fetched, to restore RTI-ACT-001 and RTI-ACT-002 to VERIFIED.
authority: India Code. If India Code cannot serve the Act, the alternative official publisher is UNKNOWN and becomes an open question rather than a guess.
method: indiacode.nic.in, navigating from its Central Acts listing. Do not reconstruct a bitstream path by editing the one that failed.
legal_basis: Published primary legislation. Not an application.
notes: SEQUENCE 0 so this precedes FQ-001 without renumbering the queue. Every deadline in this queue is computed from RTI Act timelines that are currently UNVERIFIED: s.7(1) thirty days, the s.7(1) proviso forty-eight hours, s.7(7) with s.11 forty days, the s.5(2) proviso thirty-five days, s.19(1) and s.19(3) appeal windows, and s.7(2) deemed refusal. The previously recorded URL https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2013/1/A2005-22.pdf was fetched on 16 August 2026 and returned HTTP 302 to a page titled 'India Code: Invalid URL or Argument(s)' containing no text of the Act. That failure is itself recorded rather than papered over. Free, needs no application, and blocks nothing while it is done.

action: Obtain every order suspending telecommunications in Central Delhi during July 2026: the order of 23 July 2026 recorded at INC-DEL-007, and any other order made in the same period. Ask for the order copies, the officer's designation, and the Review Committee's proceedings under rule 3(2) of the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024.
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Union of India, as the reported issuing authority. The Department of Telecommunications and the Commissioner of Delhi Police, as reported recipient, are alternative custodians if MHA transfers the application under section 6(3).
method: RTI application. One subject matter. Ask for the documents, not for an explanation: 'a copy of each order' and 'a copy of the Review Committee proceedings', not 'why was the internet suspended'.
legal_basis: Right to Information Act 2005. Note that Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) 3 SCC 637 requires such orders to be published, so this asks for a document the state was already obliged to make public. That is the strongest position an applicant can be in, and it should be said in the application.
notes: SEQUENCE 2, behind the preservation letters only. This is the best-shaped request in the queue and the reason is worth stating. Everything else this archive asks for is a record of what police did, which an office can plausibly say it does not hold, cannot locate, or has destroyed on schedule. This asks for a written order that certainly exists, whose author is a named office, whose legal power is cited in the reporting, and whose publication was already required by the Supreme Court. There is no honest 'no such record' answer available. A refusal is therefore as useful as a disclosure: a section 8 exemption claimed over an order the Court has said must be public is itself a documentable fact with a date on it. Do not bundle this with any question about the police action. One subject matter.

action: Retrieve an authoritative text of Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) 3 SCC 637 and record the URL actually fetched, to move PREC-SHUT-001 from REPORTED to VERIFIED.
authority: The Supreme Court of India's own judgment database, or an authoritative reporter.
method: Fetch the judgment. Do not cite it from a secondary source's citation of it.
notes: SEQUENCE 0, same reasoning as FQ-013: it costs nothing, needs no third party, and upgrades a claim this archive is relying on. PREC-SHUT-001 currently rests on the Internet Freedom Foundation's citation of the case rather than on the case. The proposition is well known, which is exactly why it is easy to leave unverified. FQ-014 leans on it.

action: Obtain the Supreme Court's order of 10 September 2026 recorded at PROC-SC-011, and the order of 18 August 2026 recorded at PROC-SC-006, from the Court's own record.
authority: Supreme Court of India. Orders are published on the Court's website; no application is needed.
method: Locate by cause title and date. PROC-SC-008 gives a cause title in the connected pellet-gun matter, W.P.(C) No. 917/2026, which is the obvious starting point.
notes: Every Supreme Court record in this archive is an outlet's account of an order rather than the order. That is a weakness across the whole supreme_court category, not a gap in one record, and it is cheap to fix because the orders are public. Getting the 10 September order would also settle whether the confidential witness portal at OQ-054 exists and where.

action: Obtain the Delhi Police affidavit dated 17 August 2026 filed before the Supreme Court, and the application of 31 August 2026 with the affidavit of Joint Commissioner Ajay Krishna Sharma, from the Court's own record. Then ask Delhi Police, under the Right to Information Act, for the standard operating procedure governing the Facial Recognition System, the record of what was captured at Jantar Mantar between 20 and 26 July 2026, the retention period applied to it, and the verification protocol the force says is pending.
authority: Supreme Court of India for the filings. Commissioner of Police, Delhi, through the Ministry of Home Affairs route, for the procedure and retention.
method: The filings are on the Court's record and need no application. The RTI goes to rtionline.gov.in. Ask for the procedure and the retention period, not for the list: a list of 2,873 named people is the last thing this archive should hold or ask to be published.
cost: Rs 10 application fee for the RTI; the filings are free
legal_basis: Published judicial record; Right to Information Act for the procedure and retention.
notes: The highest-value open item on the Delhi record. The Supreme Court's order of 1 September 2026 closed every FIR in the country over these protests except the one built on this list, so the list is now the whole of the live criminal exposure arising from the protest, and an Indian Express check of 205 names on it found at least 25 people who were in jail on the day the software placed them at Jantar Mantar. Two things follow that an RTI can reach. What the retention period is, because a crowd capture of everyone present is held somewhere under some rule. And what the verification protocol is, because the force told the Court verification was pending, which means the list went in before it existed.

action: Obtain the Supreme Court's orders of 28 July 2026 (PROC-SC-012), 3 August 2026 (PROC-SC-013) and 1 September 2026 (PROC-SC-014) from the Court's own record.
authority: Supreme Court of India. Orders are published on the Court's website; no application is needed.
method: Locate by cause title and date. PROC-SC-014 gives the cause title Yashovardhan Azad and Others v. Union of India and Others; PROC-SC-008 gives W.P.(C) No. 917/2026 in the connected pellet-gun matter.
notes: The 28 July order is the one to get first, and not because it is the earliest. It is reported to direct police to preserve CCTV footage, drone recordings and call logs, which is the same class of record the four preservation letters on this site ask for. A letter that can cite a court order directing preservation is asking a different question from a letter that cannot, and the order is free and public.

action: Obtain the written instruments behind the state withdrawals and the permission refusals: the Bihar Home Department notification recorded at INC-BIH-007, the Assam notification at INC-ASM-001, the order or direction by which Maharashtra withdrew, and the notice refusing permission for the Kochi gathering recorded at INC-KER-001.
authority: Bihar Home Department; Assam Home and Political Department; Maharashtra Home Department; Commissioner of Police, Kochi City, for the Ernakulam Town South refusal.
method: One RTI application per state, each asking for the instrument by its reported date and for the file noting behind it. Kerala and Maharashtra both offer online filing; Bihar and Assam should be checked before assuming it.
cost: Rs 10 per application plus copying charges
legal_basis: Right to Information Act. None of these is an investigation record, so the usual refusal ground is weaker than it is for a case diary.
notes: This is the cheapest route to a named author anywhere in this archive, and it exists only outside Delhi. A lathi charge leaves no order; a refusal of permission and a withdrawal of cases are both written by somebody, carry a date, and sit in a file that survives the news cycle. Bihar and West Bengal are both reported to have used the same cut-off, 6 pm on 26 July 2026, which is an odd coincidence between two states and is itself worth asking about: the file noting should say where the line came from.

action: Obtain the section 163 BNSS order in force across New Delhi district on 2 October 2026 recorded at INC-DEL-012, with its date, its signatory, the area and hours it covered and the ground it states.
authority: Delhi Police if the order is theirs; the Government of NCT of Delhi if it is the government's. The sources disagree (INC-DEL-013), so the first step is to ask the office that the more credible account points to and rely on a transfer under section 6(3) of the Right to Information Act if it is the wrong one.
method: RTI application, one subject matter: a copy of the order. Do not ask why it was made.
cost: Rs 10 application fee on the Union portal (RTI-UNION-002). The Delhi government fee and route are not established in this archive.
legal_basis: Right to Information Act 2005. An order made to bind the public is not an investigation record.
notes: A prohibitory order is made to be obeyed by the public, so it has to be knowable. A refusal to disclose it would be as useful a finding as the order.

action: Obtain any order suspending telecommunications in the Jantar Mantar area on 2 October 2026, the officer's designation, and the Review Committee proceedings under rule 3(2) of the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024, as for FQ-014.
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs as the issuing authority for the July order; the Department of Telecommunications and the Commissioner of Delhi Police as alternatives. Whether the same office acted on 2 October is not established.
method: RTI application, one subject matter, asking for the documents and not for an explanation.
legal_basis: Right to Information Act 2005; Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) 3 SCC 637 requires such orders to be published.
notes: Rests on a single report that a suspension happened (INC-DEL-015). If no order exists, the answer to the application says so, and that is a documentable fact with a date.

action: Two applications. First, a copy of the First Information Report registered at Shivaji Park police station on 3 October 2026 (INC-MAH-003). Second, a copy of the written refusal of permission for the gathering of 2 October 2026, with its date and signatory.

method: Separate applications, because the Maharashtra Right to Information Rules 2026 allow one subject matter per application and about 150 words (RTI-MAH-003). The portal is rtionline.maharashtra.gov.in; check that a Mumbai Police application can be filed there before assuming it.

notes: The FIR settles who is named and who complained (INC-MAH-004). The refusal is the instrument with an author, and is the Maharashtra counterpart of the Kochi notice at FQ-019.
